newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines city strikes in protest at peso woes.
newsitem.headline: Philippines city strikes in protest at peso woes.

text.p: Hundreds of commuters were stranded early on Monday as striking drivers brought public transport to a halt in this southern Philippine city, police said.

Government vehicles were pressed into service to ferry people to work after 97 percent of public utility vehicles in the city stayed off the roads in protest against the de-facto devaluation of the peso, traffic police officer Fulgencio Balucan said.
"Iligan was transformed into a ghost town," a businessman said, describing the deserted streets in the predominantly Christian city of 300,000 people.
The strike prompted the suspension of school classes while half of the city's businesses remained closed.
Transport in several other towns, including Lanao del Norte and neighbouring Misamis Oriental, were also affected by the strike which was organised by labour groups on Mindanao island, police said.
Leftist groups have threatened to launch mass action in all parts of the country today to protest against the economic policies of President Fidel Ramos.
Two weeks ago, the Philippine central bank succumbed to relentless speculative attack on the peso and allowed the currency to trade in a wider range versus the dollar, effectively a devaluation.
Ramos was scheduled to deliver to Congress later on Monday a report of his accomplishments since he assumed power in 1992.
